- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — reduce initial forecast peaks.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or low (especially <0.2) — adjust downward bias in early periods.
- Overshoot after sharp sentiment spikes — cap forecast peaks at 1.2x recent high or 1.5x 14-day moving average.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5x recent 7-day high, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Lagged overreaction: if true outcome drops sharply after forecast peak, reduce next forecast by 5–15% to avoid “overcorrection” lag.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate when sentiment is volatile (±0.25+ in 3-day window) — apply smoothing filter or reduce volatility weight.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment >0.4 for 3+ days, forecast should be capped at 1.1x recent 14-day average to avoid “sentiment inflation.”
